q: Who directed the 2005 film of Rent?
fact: Columbus also directed Home Alone, Mrs. Doubtfire, and the first two Harry Potter films.

q: Who wrote the music, lyrics, and book of Rent?
fact: Larson spent seven years writing Rent.

q: Jonathan Larson died suddenly in 1996, the night before what?
fact: He was 35. The cause was an undiagnosed aortic dissection.

q: Rent is a modern retelling of which opera?
fact: Puccini's La Bohème follows poor young artists in 1830s Paris. Mimi keeps her name from the opera.

q: How many minutes are in a year, according to “Seasons of Love”?
fact: 365 days × 24 hours × 60 minutes. It's also the score in this game.

q: In “Seasons of Love,” which of these is NOT one of the ways to measure a year?
fact: The song lists everyday ways to count a year before landing on its answer: love.

q: How does “Seasons of Love” finally say to measure your life?
fact: It's the heart of the song, and of the whole show.

q: Which song opens the film, with the cast lined up on an empty stage?
fact: The film opens on an empty theater stage. In the stage show, the song opens Act Two.

q: On what date does the story begin?
fact: Christmas Eve, 1989. The story covers one year, ending the following Christmas Eve.

q: In what neighborhood of New York is Rent set?
fact: Alphabet City in the East Village, around Avenue B and Tompkins Square Park.

q: What is Mark's passion?
fact: Mark films his friends with his camera all year. His footage becomes the film's finale.

q: What is Roger's dream before he dies?
fact: His solo about it is “One Song Glory.”

q: What is Roger's last name?
fact: Roger Davis, played by Adam Pascal.

q: What is Mark's last name?
fact: Mark Cohen. His mom keeps leaving messages on the answering machine.

q: What is Mimi's last name?
fact: Mimi Marquez, played by Rosario Dawson.

q: What is Angel's full name?
fact: Angel Dumott Schunard, played by Wilson Jermaine Heredia.

q: What is Benny's full name?
fact: Benjamin Coffin III, played by Taye Diggs.

q: What is Joanne's last name?
fact: Joanne Jefferson, played by Tracie Thoms.

q: What is Maureen's last name?
fact: Maureen Johnson, played by Idina Menzel.

q: What is Tom Collins's line of work?
fact: Collins was expelled from MIT for his theory of actual reality, and now teaches.

q: What does Joanne do for a living?
fact: Joanne is a lawyer. She ends up running the sound for Maureen's protest.

q: What does Maureen do?
fact: Her protest piece is “Over the Moon.”

q: Where does Mimi dance?
fact: It's where she performs “Out Tonight.”

q: What does Benny want to build on the lot?
fact: He'd have to clear out the homeless people living there first, which is what Maureen protests.

q: Who is Benny married to?
fact: She's one of the Westport Greys. Mark calls her “Muffy.”

q: How do Mark, Roger, and Benny know each other?
fact: Benny used to live in the loft. Now he owns the building and wants rent.

q: Who left Mark for Joanne?
fact: Mark and Joanne bond over it in “Tango: Maureen.”

q: What was the name of Roger's girlfriend before Mimi?
fact: April took her own life after learning she was HIV-positive. Roger hasn't left the loft much since.

q: What melody keeps showing up on Roger's guitar?
fact: It's borrowed from Puccini's La Bohème.

q: Who finds Collins after he's mugged?
fact: It's how Collins and Angel meet.

q: How did Angel earn $1,000 in “Today 4 U”?
a: By drumming nonstop until a dog jumped out a window
fact: Evita the Akita.

q: What was the dog's name in “Today 4 U”?
fact: Evita the Akita.

q: What is Angel's motto?
a: Today for you, tomorrow for me
fact: Angel says it while flashing the cash from the dog job.

q: What is the name of Maureen's protest piece?
fact: She gets the whole crowd to moo along.

q: What is the name of the cow in Maureen's protest?
fact: Elsie the cow jumps over the moon.

q: Why does Maureen call Mark at the start of the film?
a: To fix the sound for her protest
fact: He shows up to help and meets Joanne, who's running the sound.

q: Where does everyone go to celebrate after the protest?
fact: They take over the café and launch into “La Vie Bohème.”

q: Which song is this café scene?
fact: A toast to bohemian life, with Benny watching.

q: In “La Vie Bohème,” what does Mark say the opposite of war is?
fact: It's one of the toasts Mark makes during the song.

q: Where does Collins dream of opening a restaurant?
fact: He sings about it on the subway in “Santa Fe.”

q: What does Collins reprogram an ATM to do?
a: Pay out to anyone who enters A-N-G-E-L
fact: Collins calls it redistributing the wealth.

q: What is the name of the support group the friends attend?
fact: Angel, Collins, Mimi, and Roger all attend. The group's song is “Will I?”

q: Which song do Roger and Mimi sing when they first meet?
fact: Mimi knocks on Roger's door asking him to light her candle.

q: Who are these two?
fact: Adam Pascal and Rosario Dawson.

q: Which song does Mimi perform at the club?
fact: Mimi's big solo number, and Rosario Dawson's showcase.

q: Which song is Roger and Mimi's big fight?
fact: Roger pushes her away, and Mimi answers him with the show's motto.

q: Which song do Collins and Angel sing to each other?
fact: Collins and Angel's love song, reprised by Collins at the funeral.

q: Which song do Mark and Joanne dance through?
fact: Two exes of the same woman, learning to tango.

q: Which duet is Maureen and Joanne's blowout fight?
fact: Idina Menzel and Tracie Thoms, belting.

q: Which song does Collins sing at Angel's funeral?
fact: Jesse L. Martin's reprise is a highlight of the film.

q: Who pays for Angel's funeral?
fact: A turning point for Benny with the group.

q: Which main character dies?
fact: Angel dies of AIDS-related illness in the second half of the film.

q: Where does Roger go after leaving New York?
fact: He comes back after realizing he has to finish his song for Mimi.

q: What song does Roger finally write?
fact: He sings it to Mimi at the end. Then she wakes up.

q: In which duet do Mark (in New York) and Roger (in Santa Fe) both have a change of heart?
fact: Mark quits Buzzline and Roger heads home to finish his song.

q: What job does Mark finally quit?
a: Shooting for the TV tabloid Buzzline
Waiting tables at the Life Café
fact: He quits to finish his own film.

q: Who plays Buzzline producer Alexi Darling?
fact: Her phone calls get more and more desperate.

q: In “Tango: Maureen,” what pet name does Mark say Maureen used to call him?
fact: Mark compares notes with Joanne about Maureen while they tango.

q: What is the show's motto?
fact: It's what Roger finally takes to heart.

q: Who wrote the screenplay?
fact: Chbosky also wrote The Perks of Being a Wallflower.

q: Whose production company co-produced the film?
fact: Tribeca co-produced with Chris Columbus's 1492 Pictures.

q: What year did Rent premiere on Broadway?
fact: It moved to the Nederlander Theatre in April 1996, after selling out Off-Broadway.

q: Where did Rent first play Off-Broadway?
fact: A small East Village theater. Word of mouth sent it to Broadway within months.

q: Which major prize did Rent win in 1996?
fact: It also won the Tony for Best Musical.

q: About how long did Rent's original Broadway run last?
fact: It closed in September 2008 after more than 5,000 performances.

q: Which two main roles were NOT played by original Broadway cast members?
fact: Rosario Dawson and Tracie Thoms joined six original Broadway stars.

q: Which film actor won a Tony for originating their role on Broadway?
fact: Heredia won Best Featured Actor in a Musical for Angel in 1996.

q: Which two Rent stars were later married to each other?
a: Jesse L. Martin and Idina Menzel
fact: They met in the original Broadway company.

q: Idina Menzel later voiced which Disney character?
fact: From Maureen to “Let It Go.”

q: Jesse L. Martin became famous as a detective on which TV show?
fact: He played Detective Ed Green, then Joe West on The Flash.

q: What other Jonathan Larson musical became a 2021 film?
fact: Directed by Lin-Manuel Miranda, starring Andrew Garfield as Larson.

q: What was the film's US release year?
fact: It opened on November 23, 2005, the day before Thanksgiving.

q: This actor played which character?
fact: Anthony Rapp, who also originated Mark on Broadway.

q: This actor played which character?
fact: Adam Pascal, Broadway's original Roger.

q: This actor played which character?
fact: Rosario Dawson. Sin City came out the same year.

q: This actor played which character?
fact: Jesse L. Martin, Broadway's original Collins.

q: This actor played which character?
fact: Wilson Jermaine Heredia, who won a Tony for the role.

q: This actor played which character?
fact: Idina Menzel, Broadway's original Maureen.

q: This actor played which character?
fact: Tracie Thoms, new to the role for the film.

q: This actor played which character?
fact: Taye Diggs, Broadway's original Benny.

q: Who is this, in her “Over the Moon” catsuit?
fact: Idina Menzel as Maureen, getting ready for the protest.

q: Which song does Mimi sing, joined by Roger, as their relationship falls apart?
fact: It plays over a montage of the couples drifting apart through the seasons.
